data.long_meaning: Divi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'diva' meaning 'heavenly', 'sky' or 'day'. It is also the name of the goddess of the sun, Diva-Shakti or Aditya-Shakti. In Hinduism, the sun is considered a powerful and auspicious symbol of life, energy, and enlightenment. The name Divi carries the meaning “Heavenly” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Divi usually hope their child will grow to embody heavenly and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The sun is an essential element in Hinduism, representing power, energy, and life-giving force. Divi is a beautiful and meaningful name for a child, evoking images of warmth, vitality, and brightness.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Divi is rooted in the Hindu belief that the Sun God, represented by the goddess Diva-Shakti or Aditya-Shakti, brings enlightenment and illumination to the world. Divi is a reminder that within each one of us lies the potential for inner radiance and illumination, just as the sun brings light to the world. The name fosters a deep connection with the divine, inspiring individuals to seek inner beliefs, wisdom, and knowledge.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Divi: Radiance of the Divine. A name signifying inner illumination and divine grace.

historical_references.reference: Divi was the name of the first Jain Tirthankara of the present era, also known as Mahavira. He is believed to have lived from 597 to 527 BC in Magadha, India.

Divi was also the name of a Hindu goddess, the presiding deity of the Divi Nagar temple located in Porbandar, Gujarat, India. She is believed to have been the mother of the Hindu god Rama and wife of King Dasharatha.
